title: REDEEMing Modality Information Loss: Retrieval-Guided Conditional Generation for Severely Modality Missing Learning

problem.claim: Multimodal learning must handle scenarios where modalities are missing during training or inference because of sensor failures, data corruption, or privacy concerns.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often focus on robustness under missing modalities without reconstructing them and rely on static, sample-agnostic prompt tuning, limiting effectiveness under severe modality missing conditions.

contributions.claim: REDEEM is a retrieval-guided conditional generative framework for alleviating modality missing problems in pre-trained Multimodal Transformers.
The framework adaptively retrieves relevant instances for modality-complete and modality-incomplete samples, then uses retrieved data as experts for within-modal reconstruction of missing modalities.
REDEEM generates sample-aware inter-modal prompts from retrieved instances to guide Multimodal Transformers under severe modality missing.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe REDEEM as a novel framework and identify its adaptive retrieval mechanism as new.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report comprehensive experiments on three diverse multimodal classification benchmarks.
The authors report that REDEEM significantly outperforms competitive baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal learning commonly assumes complete modality availability during training and inference.
Real-world failures, corruption, and privacy constraints make complete modality availability impractical.
Existing missing-modality approaches do not adequately reconstruct missing modalities and use static prompt tuning, weakening severe-missing-modality performance.
REDEEM retrieves relevant examples, reconstructs missing modalities from remaining modalities and retrieved experts, and produces sample-aware inter-modal prompts.
The authors report superior performance over competitive baselines on three multimodal classification benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The method combines adaptive retrieval, within-modal reconstruction, and sample-aware prompting to address severe modality missing.

interpretation.claim: Retrieval can provide instance-specific information for both reconstructing missing inputs and conditioning downstream multimodal models.

application.claim: For multimodal systems exposed to incomplete inputs, consider using retrieved analogous instances as conditional support rather than relying only on static prompts.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported multimodal classification benchmarks or across specific missing-modality patterns.

unknowns: The benchmark names, modality types, missingness settings, and quantitative results are not provided.
The retrieval criteria, reconstruction objective, prompt construction details, and baseline configurations are not specified.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported performance.
